items.t: In Metrotown, houses sold at a median of $1,950,000 across 16 sales, and the middle half closed between $1,873,250 and $2,384,500. The median house sat 28 days and sold for 92.3% of list.
Metrotown: 31 townhomes sold at a median of $979,000, with the middle half between $734,000 and $1,142,500. The median townhome took 39 days to sell and closed at 97.2% of list.
410 condos sold in Metrotown at a median of $690,000 (middle half $580,000 to $815,750). A typical condo in Metrotown spent 31 days on the market and closed at 97.0% of the asking price.
In Metrotown, duplexes sold at a median of $1,599,900 across 11 sales, and the middle half closed between $1,546,940 and $1,735,000. The median duplex sat 15 days and sold for 98.8% of list.

How Metrotown compares with the rest of Burnaby South

items.t: Houses in Metrotown have the 4th highest median of 13 Burnaby South sub-areas, $1,950,000. Greentree Village is lowest at $1,465,000 and Deer Lake highest at $2,900,000. Central Park BS ($1,925,500) sits just below and Burnaby Hospital ($2,010,000) sits just above.

Of 8 Burnaby South sub-areas with 5 or more townhome sales, Metrotown ranks 4th highest at $979,000; the range is $840,000 (South Slope) to $1,390,000 (Oaklands). Highgate ($920,000) sits just below and Greentree Village ($980,000) sits just above.
Condos in Metrotown have the highest median of the 5 Burnaby South sub-areas, $690,000, ahead of Forest Glen at $640,000; the lowest is Central Park BS at $527,000.

Of 8 Burnaby South sub-areas with 5 or more duplex sales, Metrotown ranks 5th highest at $1,599,900; the range is $1,500,000 (Highgate) to $1,751,800 (Central Park BS). Burnaby Lake ($1,558,000) sits just below and Burnaby Hospital ($1,695,000) sits just above.

blocks.text: By build year, duplexes are the newest homes selling in Metrotown (median 2025) and houses the oldest (median 1986), a gap of 39 years.
